claude-3-haiku.basis: Dense ~20B parameter model, optimized for speed.

claude-3-opus.basis: Dense ~175B parameter model. Full parameter activation per token.

claude-3.5-haiku.basis: Estimated. Claude 3.5 Haiku is faster/smaller than 3.5 Sonnet (~20B). Jegham et al. (2025) listed in infrastructure table but did not publish energy figures. Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-3.5-sonnet.basis: Dense ~70B, improved efficiency over Claude 3 Sonnet. No Jegham measurement. Most widely deployed Anthropic model; flagged as priority for Tier upgrade in v0.2.5.

claude-3.7-sonnet.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 2.781 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.14, AWS). Ranked highest in eco-efficiency among large models. Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

claude-3.7-sonnet-thinking.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) Extended Thinking variant. Auto-detected in v0.2.4 via thinking={type:enabled} kwarg. ~2x more energy than standard claude-3.7-sonnet. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.14 (AWS). Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

claude-haiku-4-5.basis: Estimated. Claude Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). No Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-3.5-haiku energy values as the nearest lightweight Anthropic class. Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-opus-4-5.basis: Estimated. Claude Opus 4.5. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-3-opus (nearest Opus-class entry). Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-opus-4-6.basis: Estimated. Claude Opus 4.6. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-3-opus (nearest Opus-class entry). Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-opus-4-7.basis: Estimated. Claude Opus 4.7. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-3-opus (nearest Opus-class entry). Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-opus-4-8.basis: Estimated. Claude Opus 4.8. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-3-opus (nearest Opus-class entry). Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-sonnet-4.basis: Estimated. Claude Sonnet 4 (distinct from Claude 3.5 Sonnet). No Jegham measurement. Proxied from Claude 3.5 Sonnet values (similar architecture class and pricing). Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-sonnet-4-5.basis: Estimated. Claude Sonnet 4.5. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-sonnet-4 (same Sonnet class). Efficiency direction vs Sonnet 4 is uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

claude-sonnet-4-6.basis: Estimated. Claude Sonnet 4.6 (claude-sonnet-4-6). No published energy figures or Jegham measurement. Proxied from claude-sonnet-4 (same Sonnet class). Efficiency direction vs Sonnet 4 is uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

deepseek-r1.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 29.0 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.27, DeepSeek own servers). Most energy-intensive in benchmark. Short is very high — short prompts trigger maximal thinking overhead. Registry values divided by 1.27 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

deepseek-v3.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.27 (DeepSeek own servers). Registry values divided by 1.27 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gemini-1.5-pro.basis: MoE architecture (~500B total, ~100B active per token).

gemini-2.0-flash.basis: Tier 3 - Google Environmental Report (Aug 2025) gives a full-stack median Gemini Apps text-prompt anchor of 0.24 Wh, not per-token coefficients. Values here are a provisional reverse-engineering assuming 1600 token median (800 in, 800 out), PUE 1.10, and 3:1 output/input ratio. If the median prompt is shorter (e.g., 400 tokens), coefficients could be ~4x higher. Cloud-optimized hyperscale batching; long context (>128k): +40% due to KV-cache memory pressure. Treat as order-of-magnitude until Google or independent work publishes per-token Gemini measurements. Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/infrastructure/measuring-the-environmental-impact-of-ai-inference/

gemini-2.5-flash.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 2.5 Flash. Value proxied from Gemini 2.0 Flash (same order of magnitude). Efficiency direction vs 2.0 Flash is uncertain — increased capability may offset architectural gains. Use VETCH_REGION + live grid data for any carbon commitments. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-2.5-pro.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 2.5 Pro. Value proxied from Gemini 1.5 Pro (same frontier MoE tier). Efficiency direction vs 1.5 Pro is uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-3-flash.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 3 Flash. Proxied from gemini-2.5-flash (nearest Flash-class entry). Google reports large year-over-year efficiency gains for Gemini, so this proxy may overstate; direction uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-3.1-flash-lite.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite. Proxied from gemini-2.5-flash scaled down ~0.5x for the lighter Lite class. Direction uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-3.1-pro.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 3.1 Pro. Proxied from gemini-2.5-pro (same frontier MoE Pro tier). Direction uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-3.5-flash.basis: Estimated. No published energy figures or Jegham measurement for Gemini 3.5 Flash. Proxied from gemini-2.5-flash (nearest Flash-class entry). Direction uncertain. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gemini-3.6-flash.basis: Estimated proxy, not a measurement. Google's model card, published 2026-07-21, says Gemini 3.6 Flash is based on Gemini 3.5 Flash and is more token-efficient, but discloses no Wh/token, parameter count, architecture, serving hardware, or quantization. Proxied from gemini-3.5-flash; fewer tokens per task reduce total estimated energy through observed usage but do not justify changing energy per token. Tier 3 ±1000%. Source: https://deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-3-6-flash/

gemma-4-31b-it.basis: Standardized BF16 proxy for relative comparison, not representative self-hosting energy. Gemma 4 31B is a 30.7B dense Apache-2.0 model, but Google publishes no Wh/token figure. Values scale the llama-3-70b proxy (0.12/0.30 Wh per 1k tokens, pre-PUE) by 30.7/70. Published Gemma 4 benchmarks show energy varies materially with hardware, precision, context, batching, and serving engine, so deployments should replace this with a Tier-0 local calibration. Tier 3 ±1000%. Model source: https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/model_card_4 ; measurement guidance: https://ml.energy/data/

gpt-3.5-turbo.basis: Dense architecture (~20B), optimized batching. Active = total for dense models.

gpt-4.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 6.512 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). No long-prompt measurement available. Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4-turbo.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured via API observation. Short/medium cost nearly equal — GPT-4 Turbo lacks efficiency gains of newer architectures. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4.1.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4.1-mini.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 0.847 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4.1-nano.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 0.271 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). Most energy-efficient model in benchmark. Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4.5.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Very high — comparable to o3. Not a typo. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4o.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) 'How Hungry is AI?' - Hardware measurements in commercial datacenters. Non-linear model: short (<1k tokens), medium (1k-5k), long (>5k). Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4o-mini.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported: short 1.684 Wh, medium 1.418 Wh, long 2.106 Wh (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). Previously Tier 3 at 0.10/0.30 (3.5x underestimate). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-5.basis: Estimated. No Jegham measurement. Proxied from GPT-4.1 medium values (same price tier, similar MoE architecture). URI AI lab (2025) measured ~18.9 Wh average per ChatGPT-5 response but methodology is indirect (total system power × response time). Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5-mini.basis: Estimated. Proxied from GPT-4.1-mini medium values (similar price tier and architecture class). Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5-nano.basis: Estimated. Proxied from GPT-4.1-nano medium values (similar price tier and architecture class). Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5-pro.basis: Estimated. Reasoning variant of GPT-5. Proxied from o1 medium values (similar price tier, reasoning architecture). Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.1.basis: Estimated. Same price as GPT-5, assumed same compute class. Proxied from GPT-4.1 medium values. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.2.basis: Estimated. Priced ~40% above GPT-5, scaled proportionally from GPT-4.1 medium. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.2-pro.basis: Estimated. Most expensive reasoning model (12x GPT-5.2 price). Proxied from o3 medium values. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.4.basis: Estimated. Latest flagship, priced at GPT-4o level. Proxied from GPT-4.1 medium values (similar frontier MoE class). Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.4-mini.basis: Estimated. Proxied from GPT-4.1-mini medium values. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.4-nano.basis: Estimated. Proxied from GPT-4.1-nano medium values. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.4-pro.basis: Estimated. Premium reasoning model, highest-priced in GPT-5.4 family. Proxied from o3 medium values. Tier 3 ±1000%.

gpt-5.6-luna.basis: Estimated proxy, not a measurement. No model-specific Wh/token or hardware disclosure. Conservatively proxied from gpt-5.6-sol rather than inferring compute or energy from API price; actual energy may be lower. Tier 3 ±1000%. Family efficiency context published 2026-07-29: https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6-frontier-intelligence-efficiency/

gpt-5.6-sol.basis: Estimated proxy, not a measurement. No per-model Wh/token disclosure. Proxied from gpt-5.4 (frontier class, same vendor); architecture=reasoning enables reasoning-token accounting. OpenAI reported >15% better token-generation efficiency and 20% lower end-to-end serving cost on 2026-07-29, but neither figure is electrical energy and neither supports changing this coefficient. Tier 3 ±1000%. Source: https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6-frontier-intelligence-efficiency/

gpt-5.6-terra.basis: Estimated proxy, not a measurement. No model-specific Wh/token or hardware disclosure. Conservatively proxied from gpt-5.6-sol rather than inferring compute or energy from API price; actual energy may be lower. Tier 3 ±1000%. Family efficiency context published 2026-07-29: https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6-frontier-intelligence-efficiency/

llama-3-70b.basis: Dense 70B. Meta published training energy reverse-scaled for inference.

llama-3.1-405b.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Largest open-weight dense model. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.14 (AWS). Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

llama-3.1-70b.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Separate from legacy llama-3-70b entry. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.14 (AWS). Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

llama-3.1-8b.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.14 (AWS). Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

llama-3.3-70b.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). ~4x more efficient than llama-3.1-70b. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.14 (AWS). Registry values divided by 1.14 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

mixtral-8x22b.basis: MoE with 8 experts, 2 active. 141B total, ~39B active per token.

mixtral-8x7b.basis: MoE with 8 experts, 2 active. 47B total, ~13B active per token.

o1.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 12.1 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). Reasoning model with extended chain-of-thought. Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o1-mini.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Lightweight reasoning model. Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o1-pro.basis: Estimated. Extended-compute reasoning variant of o1 (10x price). Proxied from o3 medium values (similar compute class). Tier 3 ±1000%.

o3.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported medium: 21.414 Wh/1k (post-PUE ×1.12, Azure). Advanced reasoning model. 79x more energy than GPT-4.1 nano. Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o3-mini.basis: Jegham et al. (2025). Jegham-reported values post-PUE ×1.12 (Azure). Registry values divided by 1.12 to store IT equipment energy only (pre-PUE). Vetch applies PUE separately in calculate_carbon(). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o3-pro.basis: Estimated. Extended-compute variant of o3 (10x price of standard o3). Proxied from o3 medium values as floor — actual may be higher due to extended reasoning. Tier 3 ±1000%.
